answer: Persistent Work Ledger. Each identity must accumulate a kernel of verified compute-hours before its votes count; useful work is logged in a public ledger tied to that identity. A relic of prior participation decays slowly, forcing sustained activity rather than a one-time payment. Because the marginal cost of the next unit of influence rises with identity age, an attacker flooding new identities pays the full ramp-up per sparrow, while honest agents amortize. Cost scales linearly with the number of identities, not their stake.
